achievement: Left in charge of Macedon while his father King Philip II campaigned in Byzantium, crushing a Thracian revolt and founding Alexandropolis.
everyday_parallel: In the cobbled alleys of Athens, a 16-year-old boy was entering gymnasium training in wrestling, rhetoric, and hoplite formation.

achievement: Began raising an insurgent army in Magadha under the mentorship of Chanakya to overthrow the Nanda Dynasty.
everyday_parallel: In the bustling markets of Takshashila, an 18-year-old youth was finishing Gurukula studies or apprenticing in a family metalworking guild.

achievement: Claimed Caesar's inheritance against Mark Antony's opposition and raised a private legion of veterans in Italy.
everyday_parallel: A 19-year-old Roman plebeian in the Subura district worked in cramped bakeries or dockyards along the Tiber River.

achievement: Ascended the Macedonian throne after his father's assassination and forced the Greek city-states to recognize his command.
everyday_parallel: An ordinary 20-year-old Athenian male had just completed two years of mandatory frontier garrison duty (ephebeia).

achievement: Smuggled herself past enemy lines into Alexandria to form an alliance with Julius Caesar and reclaim Egypt's throne.
everyday_parallel: Along the lantern-lit alleys of Alexandria, most 21-year-old women were already married and running household looms or spice stalls.

achievement: Assumed full royal power in Xianyang, crushed a palace coup, and launched campaigns to unify China's warring states.
everyday_parallel: A 22-year-old farmer in the Wei River valley spent seasons cultivating millet and serving mandatory conscription on state irrigation canals.

achievement: Completed the Aryabhatiya in Kusumapura, explaining Earth's axial rotation, solar eclipses, and trigonometric sine tables.
everyday_parallel: In the thriving alleyways of Pataliputra, a 24-year-old artisan crafted fine cotton textiles or ivory carvings traded as far as Rome.

achievement: Led donkey caravans along the Euphrates, recording silver loans and barley contracts in cuneiform on wet clay tablets.
everyday_parallel: At 25 in Babylon, disputes over faulty copper ingots were settled at the city gate under King Hammurabi's strict commercial laws.

achievement: Governed the strategic western province of Avanti and quelled a major revolt in Taxila before becoming emperor.
everyday_parallel: An ordinary 26-year-old craftsman in Ujjain belonged to a powerful trade guild (shreni) that acted as both union and local bank.

achievement: Belonged to the literate 1% who could write hieratic script, auditing Nile grain harvests and temple rations on papyrus.
everyday_parallel: Paid in loaves of bread and jugs of beer—and already viewed as middle-aged, since average life expectancy hovered near 35.

achievement: Practiced and taught reconstructive rhinoplasty, cataract surgery, and over 120 surgical instruments along the banks of the Ganges in Kashi.
everyday_parallel: In the narrow lanes of Varanasi, a 28-year-old herbalist ground turmeric, neem, and sesame oil into poultices for travelers and pilgrims.

achievement: Renounced royal palace life in Kapilavastu and wandered into the forests as an ascetic to discover the end of human suffering.
everyday_parallel: At 29, most householders in the Gangetic plains were raising children, tending rice paddies, and maintaining household sacred fires.

achievement: Opened his own private academy in the State of Lu, teaching ethics, ritual, and governance to students regardless of noble birth.
everyday_parallel: A 30-year-old potter in Lu fired bronze-imitating ceramics in wood-kilns while paying seasonal grain taxes to local feudal lords.

achievement: Ruled an empire stretching from Greece to the Indus River before falling fatally ill in the palace of Nebuchadnezzar II in Babylon.
everyday_parallel: A 32-year-old Greek veteran in Alexandria was settling into newly built colonnaded streets, blending Hellenic and Egyptian customs.

achievement: Led Alexandria's premier philosophical academy, lecturing public officials on astronomy, geometry, and brass astrolabes.
everyday_parallel: An ordinary 35-year-old Roman citizen wrapped up shop work by early afternoon to socialize in steam-filled public bathhouses.

achievement: Witnessed the devastation of the Kalinga War, renounced military conquest, and began carving edicts of Dhamma onto stone pillars.
everyday_parallel: Travelers along the Grand Trunk Road rested at shaded wells and banyan rest-houses newly built by royal decree every few miles.

achievement: Formed the First Triumvirate with Pompey and Crassus, becoming the dominant political power in the Roman Republic.
everyday_parallel: A working-class 40-year-old in Rome lived in a noisy four-story apartment block (insula) and collected monthly state grain rations.

achievement: Drafted core statecraft, taxation, and intelligence doctrines for the Arthashastra while stabilizing the Mauryan administration.
everyday_parallel: In Pataliputra's night alleys, city watchmen enforced strict curfews and fire-safety water pots outside every timber house.

achievement: Defended the Danube frontier during the Antonine Plague while writing private Stoic reflections that became Meditations.
everyday_parallel: Reaching 45 in the Roman Empire meant you had outlived roughly two-thirds of everyone born in your same year.

achievement: Formulated principles of buoyancy, levers, and compound pulleys, designing water-screw pumps and defensive war machines.
everyday_parallel: Dockworkers in Syracuse's harbor used wooden cranes and pulleys inspired by mechanical physics to unload grain ships from Egypt.

achievement: Signed the world's earliest surviving peace treaty with the Hittite Empire and erected colossal sandstone temples at Abu Simbel.
everyday_parallel: A 52-year-old master stone-carver in Deir el-Medina was a respected village elder training younger apprentices in tomb painting.

achievement: Returned to Athens to found the Lyceum, cataloging marine biology, formal logic, ethics, and constitutional politics.
everyday_parallel: A 55-year-old Athenian elder was exempt from front-line military campaigns and spent mornings debating laws in the Agora.

achievement: Walked barefoot through Athens' marketplace questioning politicians and poets on justice, wisdom, and the examined life.
everyday_parallel: At 60, an ordinary Athenian citizen became eligible to serve as a public arbitrator settling neighborhood property disputes.

achievement: Preserved bamboo-slip genealogies and local flood records during the transition from Qin rule to the early Han Dynasty.
everyday_parallel: Reaching 65 in ancient China granted exempted status from state labor taxes and honored seating at seasonal village banquets.
